one_liner: Agner Fog's header-only C++17 SIMD vector classes for x86, with inline vector math meant to replace scalar libm loops.
what_it_does: Wraps x86 intrinsic registers (__m128/__m256/__m512) in fixed-width C++ classes such as Vec4f, Vec8i, Vec16f, Vec8d and Vec32h, with overloaded arithmetic, comparison and boolean operators, load/store/load_partial, permute, blend, lookup, gather and scatter. Optional headers add vector math (exp, log, pow, cbrt, trig, inverse trig, hyperbolic) either inline (vectormath_exp.h, vectormath_trig.h, vectormath_hyp.h) or by forwarding to Intel SVML (vectormath_lib.h). It is not a drop-in for std::cos or a loop: you rewrite the hot loop in terms of vector objects, and the same source is recompiled per instruction set (SSE2 up to AVX512-FP16), with wider classes split into two or four registers on lower sets.
how_it_is_fast: Every operator is a static inline wrapper over one or a few intrinsics, and C++17 template metaprogramming picks the cheapest instruction sequence for a given permute/blend index pattern and instruction set at compile time. Integer division by a vector-invariant or compile-time-constant divisor is replaced by multiply-and-shift (Divisor_i / const_int classes). The inline math functions use Cephes/VDT-derived polynomial approximations (Taylor polynomial for exp, Pade alternatives) with exponent-bit tricks for 2^n, and test all lanes with horizontal_and so the special-case (overflow, NaN, underflow) select path is skipped when every lane is in range; they also drop subnormal support and errno for speed.
when_to_use: x86-64 hot loops where GCC/Clang auto-vectorization fails or is fragile: branchy per-element logic, data that must be rearranged, table lookups or calls to math functions inside the loop.
Batch evaluation of exp/log/pow/sin/cos on float or double arrays where about 2 ULP accuracy, INF/NaN error signalling and flushed subnormals are acceptable.
Code that must ship SSE2, AVX2 and AVX-512 builds from one source, with runtime dispatch by compiling the same file several times (dispatch_example1.cpp, dispatch_example2.cpp).
Integer kernels dividing many lanes by the same divisor, or needing saturating, permute and lookup operations that are awkward to write with raw intrinsics.
Projects on C++17 that want a mature, single-maintainer, Apache-2.0 wrapper rather than a C++20 multi-architecture library.
when_not_to_use: Anything that must also run on ARM, POWER or RISC-V: the README and manual say there are no plans for non-x86 support and point to Google Highway instead.
Simple array loops the compiler already vectorizes; the manual itself recommends auto-vectorization when it works.

Code that needs IEEE-exact behaviour: subnormal inputs, errno, floating-point traps, pow(NaN,0) = 1, or bit-identical results across instruction sets (signed zero and out-of-range indexes differ by instruction set).

Builds that cannot take a proprietary binary: the vectormath_lib.h variant needs libsvml.a/libirc.a (Linux) or svml_dispmt.lib/libircmt.lib (Windows) copied from an Intel compiler installation; only the inline math headers are pure Apache-2.0.
Teams that need a published performance baseline: neither the README nor the 2026-09-09 manual gives any timing, hardware or compiler for the 'many times faster than scalar libraries' claim.

integration.form: header-only (plus optional instrset_detect.cpp source file for runtime CPU detection)
integration.dependencies: none for the core and inline math; optional Intel SVML (libsvml.a and libirc.a, or svml_dispmt.lib, libircmt.lib and the repo's svmlpatch.lib on 64-bit Windows) for vectormath_lib.h; optional add-on repo (containers, random, complex, quaternion, vector3d, decimal)
integration.min_toolchain: C++17 (instrset.h #errors otherwise); GCC, Clang, MSVC (VS 2019 / _MSC_VER 1920+ recommended for AVX-512; MSVC cannot target AVX512F without AVX512DQ), Intel compiler 2021+; GCC 9 and older lack some zero-extend intrinsics and are worked around
integration.platforms: x86 and x86-64 only (Windows, Linux, macOS); SSE2 minimum, up to AVX2, FMA3, AVX512F/VL/BW/DQ/VBMI/VBMI2 and AVX512-FP16, selected at compile time by -m flags or INSTRSET
integration.thread_safety: Vector objects are plain values with no shared state; the manual says containers are not safe for concurrent access and the MXCSR control word set by no_subnormals() is per thread, so each thread must set it
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: vector math overloads are named like libm (exp, log, sin, pow) but take vectors, so loops must be restructured into vector loads, operations and stores

gotchas: Inline log, exp, pow and root functions treat subnormal inputs as zero (log_special_cases for Vec8d under AVX512DQ maps a subnormal input to -INF, as for zero), never set errno or raise exceptions, and rely on INF/NaN propagation; -ffast-math, -ffinite-math-only or /fp:fast can disable that detection, and a NaN compared into a boolean vector silently becomes false.

Out-of-range element indexes, shift counts and boolean vectors holding values other than 0/-1 give instruction-set-dependent results with no error (select works bit-by-bit before SSE4.1 and on the sign bit or high byte bit from SSE4.1), so an SSE2 build and an AVX2 build of the same code can disagree.

When dispatching, vector objects must not cross between translation units compiled for different instruction sets (their representation differs); pass arrays instead. The manual's GCC flags for AVX/AVX2 include -fabi-version=0, alignment faults are possible before AVX when vectors sit in under-aligned containers, and instrset.h #undefs min/max and defines NOMINMAX on MSVC.

Open issue #91 (2026-09-28), confirmed in instrset_detect.cpp: the AVX-512 OS-support test reads CPUID leaf 0xD (what the CPU can enable, masked with 0x60) instead of XGETBV XCR0 bits 5-7, so on an OS or VM that has not enabled ZMM state the optional dispatcher can report level 9+ and the AVX-512 path faults; the leaf-7 test also uses the signed shift 1 << 31.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick VCL over EVE when you are x86-only, stuck on C++17 rather than C++20, and want explicit fixed-width classes plus Agner Fog's documented per-function ULP bounds; pick EVE or Highway for ARM. Over math_intrinsics or SIMD-math-prims, VCL gives a full vector type system and roughly 2 ULP math instead of looser approximations, but those siblings at least publish timings against libm while VCL publishes none.
verified_claims_summary: No measurement exists: the 2026-09-09 manual (section 8.3) only asserts that the inline and SVML-based vector math versions are 'many times faster than standard (scalar) math function libraries' and that VCL matches the optimization level of hand-written intrinsics, with no baseline library version, compiler, flags or CPU. A WebSearch this session also found no independent VCL-versus-libm, SLEEF or SVML timing.
status_note: Actively maintained by Agner Fog (version 2.02.04, 2026-09-09; 1.5k stars, 156 forks) and Apache-2.0 header-only, so easy to vendor, but the speed claim is tier D with no benchmark, and the optional runtime dispatcher has an open AVX-512 OS-state detection bug (#91).
